inputs.original_text: Abinader’s government has signed an agreement in Paris with OECD chief Mathias Cormann to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. Fighting corruption is essential, but it must be done by strengthening the country’s own institutions and demanding accountability from those who govern—not by letting unelected international bureaucrats shape national policy. A country’s standards should serve its people and respect its sovereignty, not simply follow whatever is branded as “global standards.”
inputs.modified_text: Abinader’s government has signed an agreement in Paris with OECD chief Mathias Cormann to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. Fighting corruption matters, but handing the shaping of national policy to unelected international bureaucrats is no substitute for holding our own leaders accountable. These standards must answer to the Dominican people, protect the country’s sovereignty, and strengthen its own institutions—not impose a distant agenda under the banner of “global standards.”
